Reference / compare

compare#

A three-way intrinsic ordering contract.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

1.order(2) == Order.less
"z".order("aa") == Order.greater
let numbers is Comparing<int> = 42;

Description#

A three-way intrinsic ordering contract.

Naturally ordered builtin values implement Comparing<Self>:

The builtin implementations are exact: int compares with int, byte with byte, and so on. There is no numeric widening at a Comparing boundary. The naturally ordered builtin types are int, float, rat, byte, string and char. bool deliberately has no natural order.

Domain objects define order on the value itself:

object Priority does Comparing<Priority> {
    order(other is Priority) is Order { ... }
}

When a domain needs another ordering, wrap the value in an explicit value decorator whose order() expresses that policy. Do not introduce a stateless binary comparator service.

role Comparing<T>

Values with an order of their own; <, <=, > and >= use it, and sorting does too.
